text.p: Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov has outlawed prostitution in the former Soviet republic, a newspaper said this weekend.
"In search of money some women and girls, the symbol of motherhood, home and peaceful life, are selling their bodies," a regional English-language weekly quoted Niyazov as saying.

"Special concern is caused by the involvement of the under-aged in this trade," said Niyazov who, according to the weekly, the Central Asian Post, also accused some Turkmen police officials of involvement in prostitution rackets.
According to the new law, those charged with prostitution would be heavily fined, with sentences of up to two years of "corrective labour" for repeat offenders.
Those caught with a prostitute would be fined and possibly jailed for up to 15 days.

Niyazov, subject of a strong personality cult, brooks no opposition from the 3.8 million population. But times are hard in the desert nation bordering Iran, driving some women to tout for clients in the capital Ashgabat's rash of glitzy new hotels.
The Central Asian Post said the law was popular but nonetheless advised women and courting couples to avoid being out late in Ashgabat.
"Local police may detain and charge them with prostitution," it said. "If you try to explain to the police that they are wrong, it will probably aggravate the case and they will extract your money."
